newShouldIssues.title: The relation digest law declares three inadmissible conditions and only two are consumed; the unannotated-field limb is enforced nowhere, while the sibling native bundle implements exactly it
selectors: foundation/check-identity.py:2070-2071 (where the native sweep IS consumed)
newShouldIssues.observed: The residueRule states: "An annotated field with no join, a join naming a field the selector does not have, and an unannotated digest/path field are each inadmissible", and the law standing states "There is no default and no residue: a new such field added without an annotation is inadmissible." Limbs 1 and 2 are genuinely consumed - the reviewer reproduced RELATION_DIGEST_LAW_RESIDUE, RELATION_JOIN_FIELD_UNKNOWN (in isolation, so the residue check cannot fire first) and RELATION_DIGEST_RETENTION, each with the shipped document passing as a positive control for all 13 relations. Limb 3 is enforced nowhere. relation_annotation_closure iterates only fields that ALREADY carry x-opensip-digest, so an unannotated field is invisible to it by construction: the reviewer injected an unannotated DigestHex, Sha256Text or CanonicalPath field into every one of the 13 relation selectors, 39 injections in total, and every single one was ADMITTED. A grep of every shipped .py outside reviews/ finds no other consumer.
newShouldIssues.thecheckThatNamesItDoesNotTestIt: check-identity.py ships a check literally named every-relation-payload-digest-and-path-field-is-annotated-and-joined, but its assertion is only that relation_annotation_closure returns non-None for each relation and that the join-bearing relation set equals {file, package, vcs-change, clones}. The reviewer reproduced that exact assertion verbatim against a document carrying an unannotated CanonicalPath field: it still evaluates True. So the authored suite passes while the property its name asserts is false.
newShouldIssues.whyItMatters: This is the guard that keeps the v8-S2 defect class closed under future editing. v8-S2 was precisely a payload field joined to nothing; the residue rule is the mechanism that is supposed to make that unrepresentable, and one third of it is inert. An implementer building from the law would implement all three limbs, the reference implements two, and two conforming implementations would therefore disagree on whether a document is admissible - which is the identical rationale that made v8-S1 a SHOULD and was accepted and fixed. The asymmetry is not a deliberate scope boundary: the native bundle implements exactly this sweep (native_digest_annotation_coverage), it is consumed and asserted at check-identity.py:2070-2071 with unannotated == [] and annotated >= 68, and the relation bundle declares the same rule with no equivalent and no stated exemption.
newShouldIssues.whyNotMust: No admissible payload can exercise it today. The relation payload schemas are closed (additionalProperties false) and the shipped document has ZERO unannotated governed fields (measured across all 13 selectors), so there is no current defect in these bytes and no runtime attack surface; adding such a field requires a reviewed design-time edit to a registered document. Identity, replay and determinism are unaffected, since any such value would still enter payloadDigest and hence fact2 - the same reason v8-S2 itself was graded SHOULD.
newShouldIssues.counterArgumentStatedPlainly: The law standing says coverage is asserted "by consumed CHECKS in the Run closure, not by counting annotations", which can be read as deliberately declining a native-style counting sweep. If that reading is intended, then the design has stated a rule its chosen mechanism cannot deliver, because an unannotated field is by construction invisible to a consumed join check. Either way the law and the enforcement disagree; the remedy differs but the inconsistency is the same.
newShouldIssues.remedy: Either (a) add the native-style annotation-coverage sweep over the relation document and consume it, mirroring native_digest_annotation_coverage, and fix the check whose name already claims it; or (b) scope the third limb explicitly as a design-time authoring rule rather than an admissibility rule, and rename the check to what it actually asserts. Either is small; what is not acceptable is leaving a normative inadmissibility claim with no consumer and a test name that asserts it.

harnessErrorsCorrectedNotCountedAsDefect: p01 classified bodyIdentity as unjoined because bodyIdentityJoin binds under the key "field", not "*Field"; and previousPath as reasonless because its reason is stated under "join". Both were reviewer classifier bugs; corrected in p02, which finds ZERO ungoverned fields.
p02 mutated FilePayloadV1 but asked relation_annotation_closure about "clones"; the function is per-relation, so nothing raised. Corrected in p03.

p03 renamed an existing join role to test limb 2, which made a real field unjoined so the residue check fired FIRST; the intended RELATION_JOIN_FIELD_UNKNOWN was reached in p04 by ADDING a bogus join field instead. An ordering artifact, not a defect.

p05 expected a RELATION_FILE* token for the borrowed-anchor owner (the intended join is RELATION_ANCHOR_FOREIGN_PATH) and for the dropped retained blob (EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE is correct and earlier). Corrected in p06.

p08 edited the FIRST semanticVersion literal, which belongs to the rust-dev-llvm closure - a field the binding deliberately EXCLUDES - so its negative version result measured nothing; and its refusal cases were masked by the fixture FIXTURE_NO_ADMISSIBLE_PAYLOAD guard. Both corrected in p09 by calling the model directly and mutating the fields the binding names.
p10 tested the healthy-universe empty view by owning an UNINVENTORIED path, which refused earlier at NATIVE_NESTED_PATH_NOT_INVENTORIED. Corrected in p11 with an inventoried non-anchor path.
p12 omitted the required --report argument for three runners, so its tamper refusals were argparse usage errors rather than pin faults. Corrected in p13 with proper arguments and untampered controls.
p14 string-matched a contract sentence that is line-wrapped in the source; confirmed present with whitespace normalised.

p15 compared the registry payloadSchemaDigest DESCRIPTION string to a hash (no self-hash cycle exists or is wanted), matched POST-CONSTRUCTION in the wrong case, and counted typed order annotations in the relation document which legitimately carries none.
p16 assumed the committed capability manifest was JSON; CVE1 is a binary encoding decoded via cve1_decode. Corrected in p16b.

p16b tested ADM-ORDER unsorted platform on a provider carrying a SINGLE platformId, where no disorder is constructible; corrected in p16c with two registered platforms and a sorted positive control, which refuses at capability.adm-order:platformIds.

p17 moved the vcs-change payload path without moving the rule atom that filters on it, so the fact stopped matching and refused at PROOF_REPLAY_MISMATCH. Corrected in p17b, which isolates the deleted-path exemption cleanly.
